interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body: Postoperative prognosis depends on the preoperative PSA and the prostatectomy findings. Extraprostatic extension is reported absent. Positive surgical margins is reported absent. Seminal vesicle invasion is reported absent. Lymphovascular invasion is reported absent. No lymph nodes were sampled; pNx does not establish node-negative disease and widens uncertainty. Postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory are needed to refine this prognosis; a future recurrence date cannot be established from surgical risk factors alone. The fixed estimated horizon is 71.94 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 43.16–100.71 months; its coverage has not been validated.

attempts.text: The prognosis is influenced by several documented factors. Favorable findings include negative surgical margins, absence of seminal vesicle invasion, and lack of lymphovascular invasion. The preoperative PSA was elevated at 13.5. Conversely, the surgical pathology revealed a Gleason 3+4 (ISUP grade group 2) and pathological stage pT2c. The absence of documented nodal sampling introduces uncertainty, as pNx does not equate to pN0. Biopsy findings were consistent with the prostatectomy specimen. The difference between biopsy and prostatectomy findings is not explicitly detailed beyond the overall pathological staging. The numeric horizon suggests a follow-up period of 71.9 months without an event. Postoperative PSA and its trajectory are critical missing pieces of information that would significantly revise this assessment.

The patient underwent a robot-assisted radical prostatectomy with a pathological stage of pT2c, negative surgical margins, and no invasion of the seminal vesicles. The preoperative PSA was 13.5. The biopsy findings showed Gleason 3+3 in both sessions, with a transition zone growth pattern. No lymph nodes were removed, and nodal status is documented as pNx, which widens uncertainty as missing nodal sampling is relevant.

The favorable surgical findings, including negative margins and absence of lymphovascular invasion, are positive prognostic factors. Conversely, the high preoperative PSA and the pT2c stage introduce risk. The difference between the biopsy grade (ISUP grade group 1) and the prostatectomy grade (ISUP grade group 2) is noted. The prognosis is guided by a heuristic horizon suggesting a time to recurrence of 71.9 months. Postoperative PSA and its trajectory remain unknown due to missing follow-up information. Information regarding postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory would significantly revise this prognosis.
